# reac-pw / fuzz_role

reac-pw's own fuzz target `fuzz_role` ([source](source/fuzz_role.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over reac-pw 1.0.42 (FreeREAC/reac-pw at f86a30a3).

Builds a PipeWire Props object from the input and parses its role key, then works out whether the requested role changes the running one, comparing the answers and the published refusal codes with the role grammar and the record of the object written. The key, the role values and the answers come from libreac's configuration header.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static library of reac-pw's nine input readers and the harness's box-model table, built from source with libreac's and PipeWire SPA's headers only; neither library is linked.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- A Props write with no role key returns 0 and leaves the caller's role unchanged ([lines 65-76](source/fuzz_role.c#L65-L76)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- 0 asks for the master and 1 for the slave, as an Int or a Float with that nearest integer; the first role key answers, and the parse returns 1 ([lines 78-89](source/fuzz_role.c#L78-L89)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Any other role value, a value that is not a number, or an object that is not a Props object returns -1 and leaves the caller's role unchanged ([lines 91-105](source/fuzz_role.c#L91-L105)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The running role asserted again is no change and is applied; the other role is a change and is pending ([lines 107-119](source/fuzz_role.c#L107-L119)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A refusal publishes its code from the shared vocabulary ("malformed"), and no refusal is "none" ([lines 121-131](source/fuzz_role.c#L121-L131)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch reac-pw` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_role.plain` | 50,952 | `ce68b4ca5b71bbc4601575772ad9658c3351be9fa76ca40233ec181edcb79e22` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_role.ubsan` | 51,696 | `c91ae9d461a2e498ced750616a27088b692b20a0f213e235ff4ba68bf2c5030b` |
| asan | `fuzz_role.asan` | 578,360 | `614cffc0864cc31d9d1ced61322c4efd567b64bc89fe09a227a05b5126e0debb` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_role.asan-ubsan` | 579,032 | `b255d4935da5af137a3967dbe33380ea43be8e78bfe05d1e356e0a2be8a69ff0` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
